Comment: Thor reconcile workflow: soft-deletes what one scan no longer saw, once per scan. Started by the scan-completion gate as reconcile-{scanId} once every manifest of the scan has finished ingestion, and before the scan's graph load, which applies these deletions to Neptune. StartRun decides per source and entity type - delete within the source's threshold, propose over it - records every decision and stages the deletions in Postgres; a Distributed Map soft-deletes each wave's windows of staged rows; Finalize drops the scan's ledger and staging. Its end - success or failure - is an execution event the scan-completion gate watches: either way the gate then starts the graph load. Terraform substitutes the placeholders with templatefile; validate edits with: aws stepfunctions validate-state-machine-definition.

StartRun.Comment: Opens the scan's reconcile row, refuses a scan still ingesting or already graph-loading, decides per eligible source and type, records each decision, stages the deletions and hands back wave zero.

MoreWaves.Comment: The loop. HasMore is true while the wave carries chunks.

DeleteWave.Label: DeleteWave
DeleteWave.Comment: One item per window of staged rows; each invocation soft-deletes its window in one transaction. Items arrive complete from StartRun and NextWave, so there is no ItemSelector. Each body holds one tenant database connection. No failure is tolerated - a window left undeleted would leave its rows in the graph - and a rerun window changes nothing twice, so the retry and a redrive are safe.

NextWave.Comment: Hands back the next wave of windows over the staged rows, or an empty one once every row is covered. Reads nothing: the wave carries the staged total.

Finalize.Comment: Drops the scan's seen-ledger and the run's staging, and closes the reconcile row - completed_with_proposals when any source was over its threshold.

RecordFailure.Comment: Closes the scan's reconcile row as failed - the one place that sees a chunk killed by its timeout. No DLQ: the gate started this run once and the row records why. A closed row, failed or not, is what lets the gate start the graph load: a failed reconcile holds nothing back.

Catch.Comment: Failing to record the failure must not swallow it; the execution still ends failed with the original error in its history.

WorkflowFailed.Cause: See the scan's reconcile workflow row for the error. Once the graph load has started a redrive is refused, so a failed reconcile is retried by the next scan.
